;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[American-led intervention in the Syrian Civil War]]
**Following the [[U.S. military]] withdrawal from [[Autonomous Administration of North and East Syria|northern Syria]], the [[United States]] is to deploy more troops to [[Syria]]'s eastern [[Deir ez-Zor Governorate]] to secure the country's [[Petroleum industry in Syria|petroleum gas]] and oilfields, according to a senior [[United States Department of Defense|Department of Defense]] official. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/10/deploy-troops-eastern-syrian-secure-oil-fields-191025022517393.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2018–19 Iraqi protests]]
**At least 40 people are killed and over 1,700 wounded when [[Iraqi Police|security forces]] violently clamp down on anti-government protestors in [[Iraq]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/10/iraqi-police-open-fire-disperse-protesters-baghdad-streets-191025075732647.html (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-50181212 (BBC News)]
*[[2019 Ethiopian riots]]
**[[Ethiopia]]n [[Law enforcement in Ethiopia|police]] report on Friday that the death toll from violent protests in [[Oromia Region]] was 67, including five officers. The protests started on Wednesday when protestors accused [[Prime Minister of Ethiopia|Prime Minister]] [[Abiy Ahmed]] of acting dictatorial, but they quickly degenerated into ethnic clashes. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/oct/25/ethiopia-protests-violence-nobel-peace-prize-prime-minister (''The Guardian'')]

;Arts and culture
*Hundreds of [[tourism in Australia|tourists]] flock to [[Uluru]] in [[Australia]]'s [[Northern Territory]] to climb it for the last time before [[Uluṟu-Kata Tjuṯa National Park|the park]]'s ban on climbing goes into effect. The ban is being implemented to respect the wishes of the indigenous [[Aṉangu]] people, who find Uluru sacred. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-australia-uluru/australias-uluru-closes-to-climbers-for-good-after-decades-long-fight-idUSKBN1X32S6 (Reuters)]

;Business and economy
*The [[United Automobile Workers]] ends their 40-day strike against [[General Motors]] after a new contract is ratified. [https://www.mlive.com/news/2019/10/uaw-ratifies-contract-ending-weeks-long-strike-against-gm.html (MLive)]
*In a move that surprised insiders, [[Microsoft]] beats [[Amazon Web Services]] to win a $10 billion [[cloud computing]] contract with the [[United States Department of Defense]]. [https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-pentagon-jedi/microsoft-beats-amazon-for-pentagons-10-billion-cloud-computing-contract-idUKKBN1X42IS?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Disasters and accidents
*[[Lion Air Flight 610]]
**[[National Transportation Safety Committee|Indonesian investigators]] conclude their probe of the disaster with the release of a 353-page final report. The report states the crash was caused by a combination of flawed software design by [[Boeing]], a failure of [[Lion Air]] to ground the jet over issues it had previously experienced, and inappropriate pilot responses to the developing emergency. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-50177788 (BBC News)]
*A car collides with pedestrians and other vehicles after running two red lights while accelerating in central [[Shanghai]]. At least five are killed and nine more injured. [https://www.scmp.com/news/china/society/article/3034535/rush-hour-smash-shanghai-kills-five-injures-nine (''South China Morning Post'')]

;International relations
*[[Brexit negotiations]]
**The [[European Commission]] announces that the [[European Union]] has agreed to a further extension of the [[Brexit]] deadline. The length of the extension is yet to be decided. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-politics-50175914 (BBC News)]

;Law and crime
*[[2019 Grays incident]]
**[[Liu Xiaoming]], [[China|Chinese]] ambassador to the [[United Kingdom]], announces he has sent a team to [[Essex]] to verify the identities of the 39 bodies found in a lorry this week, who are thought by UK authorities to be Chinese nationals. [[Post-mortem]]s are due to begin today. The [[Northern Ireland|Northern Irish]] driver remains in police custody, suspected of murder. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-essex-50177820 (BBC News)]
**It is suspected that six of the victims are [[Vietnam]]ese nationals. The family of one of them, a 19-year-old woman, made public her last text message to her parents which she sent while dying. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-50185788 (BBC News)]
**Two further people are arrested on suspicion of [[Manslaughter in English law|manslaughter]] and [[conspiracy]] to [[human trafficking|traffic people]] in connection to the case. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-essex-50179092 (BBC News)]
*[[Terrorism in Turkey]]
**Turkish police arrest nine people on terrorism charges in [[Adana]], including one foreign national. The men are suspected of [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|Islamic State]] membership, recruiting for the group, and planning terrorist attacks. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/turkey/turkey-arrests-9-daesh-linked-terror-suspects/1625951 (Anadolu Agency)]
*[[Gorny shooting]] 
**A Russian soldier shoots and kills eight fellow soldiers and wounds two others at a [[Russian Armed Forces]] base in the village of [[Gorny, Zabaykalsky Krai]]. Officials say the soldier is suspected of having a "[[nervous breakdown]]", according to [[Russian media]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-50184909 (BBC News)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019 Bolivian general election]]
**Official results announce that incumbent Bolivian president [[Evo Morales]] has achieved a great enough margin to win re-election, though the legitimacy of the electoral process has been questioned by protestors and international observers. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-latin-america-50178188 (BBC News)]
*[[2019–20 Lebanese protests]]
**[[Hezbollah]]'s [[Hassan Nasrallah]] calls on his supporters to leave the protests, warning [[Lebanese government of January 2019|the government]]'s resignation will lead to "chaos" and "civil war". It comes the day after Hezbollah supporters violently clashed with protestors in central [[Beirut]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/10/hezbollah-head-gov-fall-push-lebanon-chaos-191025131157587.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Mueller report]], [[Mueller special counsel investigation]]
**A federal judge rules the [[United States Department of Justice|U.S. Justice Department]] must provide [[United States Congress|Congress]] with [[grand jury]] information redacted from [[special counsel]] [[Robert Mueller]]'s [[Mueller special counsel investigation|investigation]] into [[Russian interference in the 2016 United States elections|Russian interference]] in the [[2016 United States presidential election|2016 presidential election]]. [https://www.wsj.com/articles/mueller-grand-jury-materials-must-be-transmitted-to-congress-judge-rules-11572034351?fbclid=IwAR0kjSMfYOkLUf7QdrojapSz3L6rporE7XC1PuQ4jATB-dNzuS_mT6L8eYU (''The Wall Street Journal'')]
*The [[Chicago Teachers Union]] 2019 strike extends into its seventh schoolday, on-par with its 2012 strike. A [[Cook County]] judge is expected to hear an emergency [[injunction]] filed against the [[Illinois High School Association]] for not allowing student athletes within [[Chicago Public Schools]] participate in state playoffs, despite the IHSA's long-standing ban against teams from striking districts. [https://wgntv.com/2019/10/25/emergency-injunction-filed-to-allow-cps-student-athletes-to-compete-in-state-playoffs/ (WGN-TV)]

;Sports
*[[2019–20 in English football]]	
**[[Leicester City F.C.]] equals the 24-year record for the biggest ever [[Premier League]] win and the biggest ever victory by an away side in an English football top-flight game after beating [[Southampton F.C.]] 9–0 at [[St Mary's Stadium]]. It was also Southampton's worst ever defeat in all competitions in their history. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/50092694 (BBC Sport)]
